messages:
alex: kicking off canary for the 'burstgate' ratecap change in eu-west-1. small percentage, will monitor. deploy-bot: rollout started for config/burstgate:v2 -> canary group 7%
oncall-bot: [ALERT] high 429 rate observed on /v1/generate (eu-west-1) — 12% error rate in last 2m
kelly-ops: seeing it too, dashboards show a sudden jump around the burstgate rollout time
maria: which rule exactly? burstgate is supposed to preserve exemption lists, right?
alex: yes that's the expectation — was a change to the sticky exemption lookup to optimize cache. should be a noop
sanjay: paging oncall — i'm live, adding myself. can you paste recent logs?
kelly-ops: log snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T14:05:23Z] rl/serve: 429 client=acct:ACCT-42 endpoint=/v1/generate rule=burstgate active=true exemptions_hit=0
[2026-03-15T14:05:24Z] rl/serve: 429 client=acct:ACCT-99 endpoint=/v1/generate rule=burstgate exemptions_hit=0
```
maria: those accounts should have exemptions. looks like exemptions lookup returned empty for many sticky keys
ops-bot: Token-accounting monitored metric: exempt_tokens_refill_rate dropped to 0 for canary nodes (eu-west-1)
alex: oh no — I didn't realize the sticky-key cache key name changed between versions. likely mismatch, exemptions not being applied
sanjay: impact: customers with reserved tokens are getting 429s. CS reporting multiple small accounts impacted, one enterprise (ACCT-42) reported errors.
cs-bot: CS alert: support-ticket #8742 opened by ACCT-42 — "generation hitting rate limit despite reserved plan"
maria: mitigation plan: 1) flip burstgate feature flag off for canary nodes 2) temporary manual exemption for ACCT-42 and other flagged accounts 3) rollback config to v1 if flag flip doesn't restore exemptions
kelly-ops: can we flip flag quickly? what's the command?
alex: run `rbctl feature disable burstgate --env=eu-west-1 --target=canary` (takes ~15s to propagate)
sanjay: doing it now — `rbctl feature disable burstgate --env=eu-west-1 --target=canary`
deploy-bot: feature flag burstgate -> DISABLED (canary, eu-west-1)
oncall-bot: [INFO] 429 rate dropping to 2% in last 1m after flag flip
kelly-ops: confirming exemptions_hit numbers back to normal on canary nodes
maria: good, but we still need to rollback the config change and prepare a patch for the sticky-key naming bug
alex: creating rollback PR to revert sticky-key rename, will push hotfix once approved.
sanjay: also create temporary token grant for affected enterprise accounts while patch ships. @cs-bot note the list: ACCT-42, ACCT-88, ACCT-19
cs-bot: manual exemptions applied to ACCT-42, ACCT-88, ACCT-19 — notified customers: yes
ops-bot: canary nodes stable; overall error rate back under 1% in eu-west-1
maria: assigning post-incident tasks: root cause analysis and release checklist gaps -> sanjay, patch owner and test owner -> alex, CS followup -> kelly-ops
sanjay: will take RCA. my initial notes: missing contract test for sticky-key backward compatibility, rollout checklist needs explicit exemption smoke test
alex: +1 add an integration test that validates exemption lookups across config versions and a canary smoke that exercises reserved-token accounts
kelly-ops: we should also add a short-circuit in rate limiter: if exemptions config reload fails, default to permissive for known enterprise accounts. create RFC?
maria: ok open RFC, but for now we avoid hacky defaults. plan: 1) hotfix PR, 2) broaden canary to a small set and run full exemption verification, 3) resume rollout only after signoff
cs-bot: CS followup scheduled for 2026-03-15T15:30Z with affected customers
alex: rolling back the canary config to v1 now (pr/rollbacks/137)
deploy-bot: rollback applied -> config/burstgate reverted to v1 for canary (eu-west-1)
oncall-bot: final check: 429 at 0.4% last 5m, exemptions_hit rates normal. closing immediate pager. :thumbsup:
maria: wonderful. leaving this thread open for RCA notes. thanks all for fast responses.
sanjay: i'll draft the incident timeline and include the command outputs and logs. tagging for postmortem: @maria @alex @kelly-ops
kelly-ops: adding monitoring alert rule to detect exemption_hit=0 spikes in future canaries
alex: lesson learned — name changes are code smell in canaryed configs. will protect next rollout with a smoke test that exercises exemption paths.
maria: action items captured. anyone want to add anything before we archive?
kelly-ops: thanks everyone. closing once RCA posted. :rocket:
